prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: low-speed head-on collision in Katy, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported back strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1122; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was traveling northbound in the left lane of a two-lane road in Katy, Texas, when the vehicle drifted across the center line and struck the front of a southbound vehicle operated by Driver 2. The impact was head-on but occurred at low speed, and both vehicles came to rest in their respective lanes. Driver 1 was seated in the driver's seat during the collision, and a Passenger was seated in the front right seat. Both occupants remained in the vehicles until emergency personnel arrived. Driver 1 reported pain in the lower back and stiffness consistent with a sudden forward and backward motion, and the complaint appears plausible given the mechanics of this impact. Driver 2 stated that the collision happened as Driver 1 described it, and two independent witnesses gave statements that match that account. Photographs taken at the scene show front-end damage to both vehicles that is consistent with the reported point and direction of impact. No prior damage to either vehicle was observed or reported. Records checked at the scene show Driver 1 is listed as a named driver on the insurance policy covering the vehicle.
